elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Neither party will assign this Agreement ... without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "IBM will not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Customer"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination right appears in the clause; condition demonstrably absent ("Any attempted assignment in violation of the foregoing will be void.")

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: "Neither party will assign ... without the prior written consent of the other party" plus Customer successor carve-out
No notice obligation appears; carve-out reads only "without consent to an affiliate or to a successor organization"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld"

offending_extra_words: Neither party will assign this Agreement or any of its rights hereunder without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld
reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: Customer affiliate and successor (including sale of substantially all assets) carve-out, mutual consent standard binding IBM, express bar on assignment to a Customer competitor, and no Vendor change-of-control termination right exists in the clause.

Minimality gate fails: operation 1 rewrites 43 words into 70 (ratio 1.63). Mutuality could have been achieved with a targeted operator swap (e.g., "Neither party"/"the other party") plus a short competitor and affiliate/asset-sale insertion rather than restating the whole first sentence.
Fallback is not independently satisfied because the written-notice mechanic for successor assignments is absent, but this is immaterial since the locked preferred level is met.
Intent preserved: the void-assignment sentence and Customer's continuing liability sentence remain untouched and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
